name: HVAC and chiller breakdown
blurb: Equipment breakdown claims from continuous maximum load operation through extreme heat.
summary: Equipment breakdown claims from continuous maximum load operation through extreme heat.

part_3_high_value_red_flags: A wear and tear exclusion that bars coverage for gradual deterioration of compressors, bearings, or coils, because continuous maximum load operation accelerates exactly that deterioration.
A corrosion or rust exclusion that would defeat claims for condenser coil failure caused by humid or coastal air during extreme heat.
An efficiency loss or gradual deterioration exclusion that treats slow loss of cooling capacity as maintenance rather than breakdown.
A consequential loss exclusion that removes coverage for spoilage of computer equipment or loss of income when a chiller fails.
A refrigerant contamination or leakage exclusion that eliminates coverage for loss of refrigerant charge or damage from refrigerant mixing.
An electrical arcing or short circuit exclusion that would bar claims for compressor motor burnout caused by voltage spikes during grid stress.
A sublimit for expediting expense or temporary cooling that is too low to rent portable chillers during a prolonged heat wave.
manuscript_wording_and_carve_backs: Delete the wear and tear exclusion for sudden and accidental breakdown of rotating equipment, and replace it with a specified maintenance warranty.
Add coverage for consequential loss including spoilage of computer equipment and loss of income caused by temperature excursion above a defined threshold.
Add expediting expense coverage for air freight of critical compressor parts and overtime labour during a cooling emergency.
Add temporary cooling coverage for rental chillers, portable air conditioning units, and fuel for backup generators without a restrictive sublimit.
Add service interruption coverage for loss of income when the utility supply to chillers is interrupted by an off premises event.
Add a refrigerant leakage endorsement that covers the cost of replacing lost refrigerant and repairing leaks, including environmental cleanup.
Add a peak season endorsement that removes any seasonal load restriction and confirms coverage while units run at continuous maximum load during extreme heat.

part_4_program_structure_and_limits.bi_waiting_period: A waiting period of twelve to twenty four hours is common for data centre cooling breakdown because even short outages cause server damage, while less critical facilities may accept forty eight to seventy two hours.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.business_interruption: Business interruption coverage should include loss of income, extra expense for temporary cooling, and an extended period of indemnity of at least ninety days to restore full cooling capacity after a major breakdown.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.property_eb_equipment: Equipment breakdown coverage should include HVAC and chiller units, cooling towers, pumps, and associated electrical switchgear, with hot testing and off premises coverage for portable rental units.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.per_occurrence_primary_excess_layered_pr: Primary equipment breakdown limits are typically set at the full replacement cost of the largest chiller plus the maximum foreseeable business income loss, with excess property layers stacked above for catastrophic cooling failure.

part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.cgl_primary: A typical primary commercial general liability limit of one million dollars per occurrence and two million dollars aggregate is common, but the actual limit is driven by lease and customer contract requirements.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.paper_basis: Occurrence based applies here because the exposure is sudden and accidental equipment breakdown causing bodily injury or property damage, not a latent professional service or gradual condition that would trigger claims made coverage.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.excess_umbrella_towers: Excess umbrella towers are typically built in five million to twenty five million dollar layers above the primary, with total limits set by the largest contractual indemnity obligation in the data centre lease or colocation agreement.

part_1_core_third_party_liability_exposu: Bodily injury to employees or contractors from refrigerant leaks, compressor explosions, or electrical arc flash during maintenance or breakdown.
Property damage to tenants or neighboring premises from water discharge, refrigerant release, or fire caused by chiller failure.
Third party business interruption claims from colocation customers whose servers overheat due to cooling loss, if contractual liability is assumed.
Environmental liability from release of ammonia or other regulated refrigerants into soil, water, or air.
Products and completed operations liability for HVAC contractors who installed or serviced the equipment, if their work is alleged defective.
Premises liability for slip and fall injuries from condensate leaks or ice formation around cooling towers.
Contractual liability for failure to maintain specified temperature and humidity levels under service level agreements.

underwriter_wants_to_know: Age, manufacturer, and maintenance history of each chiller and HVAC unit, including whether OEM service contracts are in place.
Redundancy configuration, such as N plus 1 or N plus 2, and whether cooling load can be shed without shutting down servers.
Maximum continuous load rating versus actual operating load during extreme heat events, and whether units have ever run above nameplate capacity.
Refrigerant type and charge size, including whether it is a flammable or high global warming potential refrigerant subject to environmental reporting.
Availability of critical spare parts, especially compressors and control boards, and lead times for replacement during peak cooling season.
Whether the facility has backup cooling, such as portable chillers or rental units, and how quickly they can be deployed.
Historical breakdown frequency and mean time to repair for similar units in the portfolio.
